turns.reply:
It double-charges. Stripe does dedupe its own deliveries — a replay arrives with the same `event.id` — but nothing in this handler ever looks at `event.id`. The only guard is `inFlight`, and that holds `event.data.object.id`, the payment intent, and drops it in the `finally` as soon as the request ends.

So the second delivery finds an empty set, walks into `dispatch`, and calls `capturePayment` with no idempotency key. Stripe's dedupe is on its side of the wire; it stops the same event being *delivered* twice concurrently, not the same intent being *captured* twice an hour apart.

The one thing I couldn't check from the diff is whether `capturePayment` derives a key internally — `src/payments/capture.ts` isn't in the change. If it does, this is a minor, not a blocker.

revisions.body:
A redelivered webhook can capture the same payment twice.

Stripe redelivers with the same `event.id`, but nothing here keys off it: `inFlight` holds `event.data.object.id`, the payment intent, and drops it in the `finally`. So a replay arrives with an empty guard and this line re-enters `capturePayment`, which takes no idempotency key. The customer pays twice.

Key the guard on `event.id` and pass it through as the idempotency key.
